Farmers & Merchants Bancorp, Inc. Reports
2026 Third-Quarter and Year-to-Date Financial Results
ARCHBOLD, OHIO, October 22, 2026, Farmers & Merchants Bancorp, Inc. (Nasdaq: FMAO) today reported financial results for the 2026 third quarter and year-to-date ended September 30, 2026, on a consolidated basis.
2026 Third-Quarter Financial and Operating Highlights
(at September 30, 2026, and on a year-over-year basis unless noted)
• 94 consecutive quarters of profitability
• Net income increased 30.3% to $11.5 million, or $0.84 per basic and diluted share
• Strong profitability drives ROAA to 1.29%, compared to 1.05%
• Net charge-offs to average loans of 0.00%
• Tier 1 leverage ratio was 9.14%
• Cost of interest-bearing liabilities improved to 2.59%, from 2.83%
• Net interest margin increased by 17 basis points to 3.57%
• Efficiency ratio improved to 58.09%, compared to 63.11%
• Third quarter regular dividend per share increased 5.5% to $0.96 annualized
• Company declared an additional $0.01 per share special dividend, bringing total third-quarter payment to $0.250 per share
Lars B. Eller, President and Chief Executive Officer, stated, “2026 is shaping up to be a historic year of profitability and growth with year-to-date earnings per share increasing 39.8% to $2.39. Throughout the 2026 nine-month period, our team has worked hard to expand our net interest margin, control operating expenses, grow our balance sheet, and maintain excellent asset quality. We are encouraged by the progress we have made across these key priorities and believe we are well positioned to sustain our positive momentum through the remainder of 2026 and into 2027.”
Income Statement
Net income for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, was $11.5 million, compared to $8.9 million for the same period last year. Net income per basic and diluted share for the 2026 third quarter was $0.84, compared to $0.64 for the same period last year. Net income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $32.9 million, compared to $23.5 million for the same period last year. Net income per basic and diluted share for the 2026 nine months was $2.39, compared to $1.71 for the same period last year.
Mr. Eller continued: “We believe F&M is well positioned to navigate a higher interest rate environment and capitalize on opportunities to further expand our net interest margin. With loan repricing opportunities extending through 2028, we believe we have a favorable backdrop to support interest income growth in the coming quarters and years. Combined
with our disciplined approach to deposit pricing and funding costs, we remain optimistic about our ability to maintain the significant improvement in net interest margin achieved over the past year.”
Deposits
At September 30, 2026, total deposits were $2.96 billion, an increase of 7.7%, or $210.6 million from September 30, 2025. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, F&M’s cost of interest-bearing liabilities was 2.59%, compared to 2.83% in the same period last year.
Loan Portfolio and Asset Quality
Total loans, net at September 30, 2026, increased 3.0%, or by $79.0 million to $2.74 billion, compared to $2.66 billion at September 30, 2025. The year-over-year increase was driven primarily by higher agricultural, commercial and industrial, and consumer real estate loans, partially offset by lower commercial real estate, consumer, and agricultural real estate loans.
F&M continues to closely monitor its loan portfolio with a particular emphasis on higher risk sectors. Nonperforming loans continue to normalize on a year-over-year basis and were $6.2 million, or 0.23% of total loans at September 30, 2026, compared to $7.4 million, or 0.27% of total loans at June 30, 2026, and $5.2 million, or 0.19% of total loans at September 30, 2025.
F&M maintains a well-balanced, diverse, and high performing CRE portfolio. CRE loans represented 48.2% of the Company’s total loan portfolio at September 30, 2026. F&M’s CRE portfolio included the following categories at September 30, 2026 (*) :

At September 30, 2026, the Company’s total allowance for credit losses to total loans was 1.08%, compared to 1.07% at September 30, 2025.
Mr. Eller concluded, “Our relationship-based banking model and local decision-making continue to differentiate F&M across our Ohio, Indiana, and Michigan markets. We maintain a healthy lending pipeline, reflecting continued opportunities to support businesses and consumers throughout our communities. Our local market knowledge and disciplined underwriting practices allow us to remain selective in pursuing new business while maintaining strong asset quality. We believe this balanced approach to profitable growth, combined with our continued focus on operational efficiency and shareholder returns, positions F&M to build upon our strong financial performance.”
Stockholders’ Equity and Dividends
Total stockholders’ equity increased 6.9% to $386.9 million, or $28.12 per share at September 30, 2026, from $361.8 million, or $26.31 per share at September 30, 2025. The Company had a Tier 1 leverage ratio of 9.14% at September 30, 2026, compared to 8.74% at September 30, 2025.
Tangible stockholders’ equity increased to $297.5 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $271.0 million at September 30, 2025. On a per share basis, tangible stockholders’ equity at September 30, 2026, was $21.62 per share, compared to $19.71 per share at September 30, 2025. Tangible stockholders’ equity and tangible book value per share are non-GAAP financial measures; see “Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures.”
F&M is committed to returning capital to shareholders and has increased the annual cash dividend for 32 consecutive years. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company declared cash dividends of $0.71 per share, representing a 6.0% increase over the same period last year. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the dividend payout ratio was 29.34% compared to 38.64% for the same period last year.
As part of F&M’s disciplined approach to capital management, the Company has continued to actively repurchase shares of F&M common stock. These repurchases are intended, in part, to help offset dilution associated with equity-based management compensation while supporting F&M’s broader objective of managing capital in a manner that enhances long-term shareholder value.
Mr. Eller concluded, “One of the most rewarding aspects of our continued financial success is the ability to share that success with our shareholders. Our 32 nd consecutive annual dividend increase, and third quarter special dividend, are testaments to the strength of our franchise, the consistency of our financial performance, and our disciplined approach to capital management. We believe the combination of profitable growth, a strong balance sheet, and consistent capital returns positions F&M to create meaningful long-term value for our shareholders.”
About Farmers & Merchants Bancorp, Inc.
Farmers & Merchants Bancorp, Inc. (Nasdaq: FMAO) is a financial holding company headquartered in Archbold, Ohio, and the parent company of The Farmers & Merchants State Bank.
About Farmers & Merchants State Bank:
F&M Bank is a local independent community bank that has been serving its communities since 1897. F&M Bank provides commercial banking, retail banking, and other financial services. Our locations are in Butler, Champaign, Fulton, Defiance, Hancock, Henry, Lucas, Shelby, Williams, and Wood counties in Ohio. In Northeast Indiana, we have offices located in Adams, Allen, DeKalb, Jay, Steuben, and Wells counties. The Michigan footprint includes Oakland County, and we have Loan Production Offices in Muncie, Indiana; and Perrysburg and Bryan, Ohio.
Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures
This release contains certain non-GAAP financial measures, including tangible stockholders’ equity and tangible book value per share. Management believes these measures facilitate period-to-period comparisons of the Company’s performance and provide useful supplemental information to investors; however, they should not be considered a substitute for, or superior to, financial measures calculated in accordance with GAAP.
Basis of Presentation
The financial information in this release is preliminary, based on management’s current expectations, and is subject to change pending completion of customary quarterly closing processes and review. Unless otherwise indicated, all figures are presented on a consolidated basis and comparisons are to the same period of the prior year. Averages may be annualized. Totals may not foot due to rounding.
